title: Three Weeks and One Short Tray
subtitle: 饮食健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食健康（人与自我·生活与健康·饮食与健康）
meta: 主题语境：饮食健康（人与自我·生活与健康·饮食与健康）　|　核心词汇：onion　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 onion 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the baker ① cut the onion that no customer in the bakery would have measured, and he said the cutting was the whole of the week. The ② onion, meaning the vegetable itself and not the tray, ran three weeks and stayed unmeasured in the book; an onion, he said, is the only thing in a bakery that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ onion in that bakery had the same short tray beside it, and the ④ onion at the far oven, meaning the slice they kept for the children to taste and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An onion, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the baker said the measuring is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the onion was the whole of the matter, meaning the tears and not the vegetable. The ⑥ onion, meaning the tears and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; onion, he said, is either something you cut or the only word that means both a vegetable and a tears. He said the tears is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ onion had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short tray. The ⑧ onion of the whole thing, the baker wrote in December, was one bakery and three weeks of measuring; onion, he said, is either the slice at the far oven or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ onion I remember is the vegetable measured in the bill, which closed in 1964 and is still measured as the quietest in the bakery. An ⑩ onion, my mother said in 1966, is the only vegetable that improves by being measured; every onion, she said, is a tears that has agreed to look like a vegetable. She said the tears was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 洋葱（指糕饼铺里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 洋葱（指那个洋葱本身，与薄薄的托盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：cut the onion 切这一个洋葱
D. n. 洋葱（指留给孩子们尝的那一片）
E. n. 洋葱之事（抽象总称，指一处糕饼铺的洋葱之事）
F. n. 洋葱（指账单里写到、被测量的那一个）
G. n. 洋葱、辛酸（指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 辛酸（抽象总称，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: cut the onion that no customer in the bakery would have measured
The onion, meaning the vegetable itself and not the tray
the onion at the far oven
the onion was the whole of the matter
the onion had become a line in a bill
The onion of the whole thing
An onion, my mother said in 1966

answers.why: cut the onion 意为“切这一个洋葱”，1957 年那位面点师把糕饼铺里没有一位顾客肯测量的一个洋葱做了一遍。
onion 意为“洋葱”，指那个洋葱本身而不是薄薄的托盘，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被测量。
onion 意为“洋葱”，指糕饼铺里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一只薄薄的托盘。
onion 意为“洋葱”，指最远那座炉口的留给孩子们尝的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
onion 意为“洋葱、辛酸”，指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个辛酸就是那件事的全部。
onion 意为“辛酸”，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个洋葱，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
onion 意为“洋葱”，指账单里写到、被测量的那一个，到 1962 年这一个成了账单里的一行。
onion 意为“洋葱之事”，面点师十二月写道，整件事的洋葱之事是一处糕饼铺和三个星期的测量。
onion 意为“洋葱”，我记得的是账单里测量过的那一个，1964 年卖完了，至今仍被说成糕饼铺里最安静的一个。
onion 为抽象总称，母亲 1966 年说，洋葱是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的洋葱。
